data.headline: Senior Software Engineer @ Coinbase | Agentic AI Acceleration, ex-Coinbase One
data.about:
Leveraging technology to build a better tomorrow.

I current serve as one of the backend tech leads of Coinbase One, Coinbase's premium subscription service, focused on the maintenance and development of the product's various benefits. During my tenure at Coinbase, I've helped scale Coinbase 20x from 20,000 to 400,000 paying subscribers. I've led several keystone benefit initiates such as Boosted USDC Rewards (offering a leading APY), Boosted Coinbase Card (rewarding users with every transaction), Advanced Trading Rebates, and Boosted Staking Rates. 

My Duke University education, where I studied Computer Science and Biomedical Engineering, underpins my innovative approach to solving complex problems. Skilled in Golang, Python, and a wide assortment of tooling, I am committed to pushing the boundaries of technology to enhance user experiences and drive financial empowerment.

projects.title: Curbing Storm Surge Inundation: Computational Fluid Dynamics Simulation for Cost and Damage Reduction in New York City Subway Stations
projects.subtitle: Sep 2015 - Jun 2016

description.text: During Hurricane Sandy, New York City received large amounts of flooding due to storm surge. With multiple days of storm surge warnings, subway preservation efforts by the Metropolitan Transit Authority failed and subway stations experienced high levels of internal flooding with unprecedented amounts of damage due to extensive water flow inundating through the sidewalk ventilation gratings. In this investigation, we have redesigned the standard ventilation grating to reduce storm surge inundation. The design implements a inverted lateral system, which can be easily closed to seal subway gratings before anticipated storm surge. The design implements modern stress resistance techniques which can prolong the lifespan of the ventilation grating. Using computer-aided design and computational fluid dynamics simulation software, the redesigned ventilation grating was virtually modeled and computationally compared to the standard design. The designs were simulated to test the day-to-day functions such as stress resistance and ventilation properties in addition to storm surge prevention. The data indicates significant differences of storm surge reduction, as the redesign reduces nearly all catastrophic water damage. The redesign underwent less deformation over time and can tolerate higher levels of stress compared to the current grating system. The redesigned grating is able to reduce nearly all damages and costs associated with storm surge inundation while retaining the important functions of a proper a ventilation grating. The redesigned grating requires one-time installation in storm surge susceptible regions of New York City and will compensate for initial costs after a single storm.
